analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. It bumps the last-updated date (line 3) and adds a clarification at the end of the `performance_measurements` table (head lines ~578-586). The clarification says sample_age_ms is the age since the newest observation, even if an older completed observation arrives later. It also says the Swift producer applies the same rule per workload bucket and per current-posture series (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.observe), and that EWMA/sample counts keep receipt order. It states the wire fields are unchanged.

The change is documentation only. It adds no code, message type, field, authentication path, encryption path, or authorization decision. The base text shows `performance_measurements` as transient routing observations, outside registration signature inputs. The existing doc says clamping and freshness on the coordinator side do not affect routing or admission. The measurement fields are provider-reported and adversarial (ADV-001, T-007), but the PR does not change how they are consumed or trusted.

No TB-002 or TB-011 boundary behavior is altered. The coordinator-to-provider WebSocket, App Attest resume, drain, and authorization sections are unchanged. No threat-model assumption is invalidated.

Remaining uncertainty: the actual Swift producer change in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift is not in the supplied evidence. The doc claim about age semantics is unverified here. The coordinator's use of these provider-reported values for deadline or capacity admission was not examined. If the Swift change alters age reporting, a malicious provider could already forge any value, so this carries no new trust implication.
